minutes.headline: Budget Task Force backed a narrowly scoped audit and health insurance opt-out research ahead of special town meeting.
minutes.summary: The task force discussed a Finance Committee idea for a deep-dive audit of town records, with the scope to be kept narrow. Most of the meeting covered town health insurance: the opt-out incentive and its rules, a high deductible plan, and retiree contribution rates. The group reviewed a one-page list of recommendations for special town meeting, dropped the Proposition 2.5 explanation from it, and no formal votes were audible.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said a vaguely described miscellaneous non-recurring line that disappeared is why a deeper audit is wanted before asking voters for more money.
The current incentive is paid only to people who first took town insurance and then dropped it, and was said to be weak against rising costs. Other communities were said to range widely.
The policy requires two years on the insurance before opting out, with individual and family amounts differing. The payout comes from the town, not the school budget, and is paid at fiscal year end.
Last year's preliminary increase was feared to be double digit but the final was lower. Trend numbers come mid to late December and real numbers in January.
Examples were given of emergency room co-pay changes with surplus paid back to employees, and gradual retiree contribution rate increases. Examples were illustrative, not proposals.
DLS data shows fees already rose significantly, so wording was shifted toward periodic fee review.
Accepting town roads that are maintained but lack documented acceptance could raise Chapter 90 funding.
The advisor suggested a top-to-bottom review of trash disposal, with possible considerable savings. Bag and cart costs were discussed.
Heating and cooling grant applications were discussed, including a phase 2 application submitted Friday.

decisions.decision: The advisor agreed to research opt-out practices and incentive levels in peer towns, expected to take about two weeks.
The advisor will raise a high deductible plan with the insurance association reps next week and ask them to cost it out.
The Proposition 2.5 and override explanation was dropped from the talking points to keep the document simple.
Next meeting set for the 4th, before special town meeting, with assessors invited and health insurance follow-up on the agenda.
